title: Collateral, Two-Way CSA, Margin Period of Risk and Netting
august: Two-way CSA; margin period of risk.

maps.tested: The margin computation is a red-herring favourite: full data is supplied, the threshold-plus-MTA test fails, and the correct answer is no call and zero.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'calculate collateral required given the values of MtM exposure, threshold, etc.'; 'overcollateralisation account balance'. The sheet singles out LO 35.g (know the terms very well), LO 35.f (disputes and reconciliation) and LO 35.j (how market, operational and liquidity risk arise through collateralisation, a role-misassignment favourite). From Reading 34, termination features and trade compression are flagged as crucial.

vardeezReading: CR-16: Very Important. "Termination Features & trade compression- These seem to be crucial here." CR-17: Very Important. "(LO 35.g - Know the terms here very well). LO 35.j This too can be imp. (LO 35.f - This is really imp abt disputes in collateral)". CR-20: Very Important. "CVA/BCVA and DVA is a favorite topic of GARP. Know the formulas very well. You cannot afford to skip this chapter at all."

selectors.name: Collateral required: threshold, MTA, rounding
selectors.what: Credit support amount (margin to call or post) from the netted MtM value, the threshold(s), MTA, rounding and the margin already held: CSA amount = max(value - K_C, 0) - max(-value - K_P, 0) - C, where K_C is the counterparty's threshold, K_P the calculating party's own threshold and C the credit support balance (negative if posted). Positive means call or request return, negative means post or return.
selectors.theory: Why the threshold leaves an uncollateralised part, why the credit support amount is not the portfolio value, that the margin already held must be netted off, that only the own threshold applies when out of the money, and that after a rating downgrade the new rating-linked threshold applies.

selectors.name: Trap: threshold plus MTA fails, no call
selectors.what: Full data is supplied but the required amount after threshold and balance is below the MTA, so no transfer is made and the correct answer is zero. Once the MTA is passed the full amount moves: the MTA is not deducted from the amount due.
selectors.theory: The MTA only decides whether a transfer happens; threshold and MTA are additive for when a call can be made; rounding is applied only after the test is passed; MTAs create path dependency.

selectors.name: Overcollateralisation: initial margin and haircuts
selectors.what: Initial margin (independent amount, a negative threshold) and haircuts as sources of overcollateralisation: required margin = max(value - K_C, 0) + initial margin; with a haircut h, value credited = (1 - h) x market value, so to deliver credit X post X / (1 - h). The securitisation overcollateralisation account is drilled in A9.
selectors.theory: Why initial margin covers the delay to default and close-out costs, that it is not netted against variation margin and not used together with a threshold, what drives a haircut size (liquidation time, volatility, credit, liquidity, wrong-way linkage), and the normal-theory haircut h = Phi^-1(alpha) x sigma x sqrt(tau).

selectors.name: Features and terms of a collateral agreement
selectors.what: Features of the CSA under the ISDA Master Agreement, CR-17 g: valuation method and timing, margin amount, transfer mechanics, eligible margin, substitutions, dispute resolution, remuneration, initial margin, haircuts, rehypothecation, triggers, and how threshold, MTA and rounding work; terms fixed at signing and changed only by mutual amendment.

selectors.name: Disputes and reconciliation
selectors.what: CR-17 f: the valuation agent (normally the party calling for margin), why collateral disputes arise (trade population, valuation methodology, application of CSA rules, market data and close time, valuation of posted collateral) and how reconciliation of portfolios and margin requirements resolves them; frequency of reconciliation and the effect on capital.

selectors.name: Risks created by collateralisation, role misassignment
selectors.what: CR-17 j: how market (including FX and wrong-way margin), operational and liquidity risk, including funding liquidity risk, arise through margin, and which party bears each: liquidation risk sits with the margin holder, funding liquidity risk with the party that must post, and a one-way CSA hurts the margin giver.

selectors.name: Termination features and trade compression
selectors.what: CR-16 d: mandatory, optional and contingent break clauses and Additional Termination Events (rating downgrade) with their benefits and dangers (cliff-edge effects, no Basel capital relief for rating triggers); trade compression as multilateral tear-up of redundant trades that cuts gross notional but not market risk, including finding the net notional and the party holding the net position.

selectors.name: Two-way vs one-way CSA, rating-linked terms
selectors.what: Differences between no CSA, a one-way CSA (only one party receives; infinite threshold for the other) and a two-way CSA (both post; typical of financial counterparties, zero thresholds standard interbank), and how threshold, initial margin and MTA are linked to credit quality (rating-linked parameters) with their problems (slow ratings, liquidity cliff effects).

selectors.name: Margin period of risk and collateralised CVA
selectors.what: MPoR as the effective time from the counterparty ceasing to post margin until all trades are closed out and replaced, its pre-default and post-default components, typical values (Basel II 10 business days, longer for large or illiquid portfolios and disputes, CCPs about 5 days) and its effect on collateralised exposure and CVA: with variation margin only, risk falls by about sqrt(maturity / MPoR) and CVA_coll = CVA_uncoll / reduction factor, with maturity and MPoR in the same units.
selectors.theory: MPoR is not the margin call frequency (daily calls, 10-day MPoR) and is not used for funding; it is a catch-all rather than the literal close-out time; it is the primary driver of the need for initial margin; high thresholds take CVA to the uncollateralised value and high initial margin to near zero; the reduction follows the square root of time, not linear time.

notSelected: CR-16 a, b and c (ISDA master agreement purpose, close-out and multilateral netting procedures, effectiveness of netting), CR-17 a, d, e, i and k (rationale for collateral management, the valuation agent role beyond disputes, collateral mechanics and types, funding, rehypothecation and segregation, regulatory capital requirements) and the CR-20 j parts beyond the margin period of risk (thresholds and initial margin in the CVA formula as a stand-alone topic) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
